items.t: Are lilies poisonous to cats?
items.a: Yes. Lilies from the Lilium genus, such as Easter, tiger and stargazer lilies, are highly toxic to cats. Any amount of the leaf, stem, flower, pollen or even the vase water can cause kidney failure. If your cat touches or chews a lily, take your cat to a vet immediately.

items.t: Can cats drink milk?
items.a: It is best not to give it. The ASPCA explains that pets do not have much lactase, the enzyme that breaks down lactose, so milk and dairy can cause diarrhea or other stomach upset. Fresh water is the drink cats need, so ask your vet before adding any new food or drink.

items.t: Can cats eat chocolate?
items.a: No. Cornell lists chocolate among human foods that are off limits for cats. Chocolate contains methylxanthines, which can cause vomiting, diarrhea, hyperactivity, an abnormal heart rhythm, tremors and seizures in pets. Darker chocolate is more dangerous. If your cat eats chocolate, call your vet or a pet poison hotline.

items.t: Can cats eat onions or garlic?
items.a: No. Onions, garlic, chives and leeks belong to the Allium family, which is poisonous to cats. Cats are more sensitive than dogs. These foods can upset the stomach and damage red blood cells, which can lead to anemia. If your cat eats any, call your vet or a pet poison hotline.

items.t: How often should I feed my cat?
items.a: It depends on age. Cornell says kittens usually do best with three meals a day until six months old, then two meals a day until they turn one. Most adult cats do well fed once or twice a day. Keep fresh water out at all times, and ask your vet how much your cat should eat.

items.t: Is Tylenol (acetaminophen) toxic to cats?
items.a: Yes. Acetaminophen, the pain and fever reducer in Tylenol and many cold, flu and allergy products, is especially dangerous for cats, says Pet Poison Helpline. It can cause stomach upset, blood problems and liver failure. Never give your cat any medicine your vet did not prescribe, and call a vet or poison hotline if your cat swallows any.

items.t: Why does my cat have diarrhea?
items.a: Often it is short lived. Cornell says a sudden diet change or stress, such as a long car trip, can cause a few days of loose stools. Diarrhea can also signal infection, inflammation, thyroid, kidney or liver disease, or cancer. Seek veterinary care soon if it lasts more than a day or two and your cat seems unwell.

items.t: Why is my cat not eating?
items.a: A cat that avoids food needs attention. Cornell explains that when cats stop eating, fat moves into the liver and can cause hepatic lipidosis, or fatty liver, which can be fatal if not treated promptly. It is more common in overweight cats and often follows another illness. Call your vet if your cat refuses food.

items.t: Why is my cat so itchy?
items.a: Fleas are one of the most common reasons cats itch. Cornell says flea bites can cause intense itching, and constant scratching can open the skin to infection. Cats with flea allergy may get red, crusty bumps. Ask your vet about flea control, because some products can harm cats if used wrongly.

items.t: Why is my cat throwing up?
items.a: Even healthy cats vomit now and then, and bringing up a hairball every week or two is not unusual, says Cornell. See your vet promptly if your cat vomits more than once a week, or if vomiting comes with lethargy, weakness, poor appetite, blood, more thirst, changes in peeing or diarrhea.

items.t: Can dogs eat chocolate?
items.a: No. Chocolate contains theobromine and caffeine, which can cause vomiting, diarrhea, panting, thirst, hyperactivity, an abnormal heart rhythm, tremors and seizures in dogs. Baking chocolate, cocoa powder and other dark chocolate are the most dangerous. If your dog eats chocolate, call your vet or a pet poison hotline right away.

items.t: Can dogs eat grapes?
items.a: No. Grapes, raisins, sultanas and currants are toxic to dogs. Pet Poison Helpline says eating them can cause vomiting, belly pain or diarrhea, followed quickly by kidney injury and kidney failure. The ASPCA also lists grapes and raisins as foods to keep away from pets. Call a vet or a pet poison hotline if your dog eats any.

items.t: Can dogs eat macadamia nuts?
items.a: No. Macadamia nuts can make dogs weak, wobbly and shaky, raise their body temperature and cause vomiting. The ASPCA says signs usually appear within 12 hours, and dogs usually recover within 24 to 72 hours. Their high oil content can also cause pancreatitis. Call your vet or a pet poison hotline if your dog eats any.

items.t: Can dogs eat onions or garlic?
items.a: No. Onions, garlic, chives and leeks belong to the Allium family, which is poisonous to dogs. They can upset the stomach and damage red blood cells, leading to anemia. Risk depends on the amount eaten, and Japanese breeds such as Akitas and Shiba Inus are more sensitive. If your dog eats any, call your vet or a pet poison hotline.

items.t: Can dogs eat raw bread dough?
items.a: No. Raw yeast dough keeps rising in a dog's warm stomach, which can cause painful bloating and, less often, a twisted stomach that is life threatening. The yeast also makes alcohol, which can cause alcohol poisoning with low blood sugar, weakness and seizures. If your dog eats raw dough, call your vet or a pet poison hotline right away.

items.t: How often should I bathe my dog?
items.a: Less often than you might think. The ASPCA says most dogs do not need a bath more than a few times a year. Regular brushing helps keep them clean in between. Before a bath, comb or cut out any mats, and rinse out all the soap so dirt does not stick to leftovers.

items.t: How often should I feed my dog?
items.a: It depends on age. The ASPCA says puppies 8 to 12 weeks old need four meals a day, three to six months old need three, and six months to one year need two. After the first birthday, one meal a day is usually enough, but larger dogs and dogs prone to bloat do better with two smaller meals.

items.t: Is ibuprofen safe for dogs?
items.a: No. Pet Poison Helpline says ibuprofen is a human pain reliever that should not be given to pets. In toxic amounts it can cause stomach ulcers with bloody vomiting or diarrhea, kidney damage and coma. Never give your dog medicine your vet did not prescribe, and call a vet or poison hotline if your dog swallows any.

items.t: Is marijuana toxic to dogs?
items.a: Yes. Pet Poison Helpline says there is no safe dose of psychoactive marijuana for pets. Eating it or breathing the smoke can cause stomach upset, stumbling, a dazed or aggressive state, sudden flinching and leaking urine. Severe cases can lead to collapse, seizures or trouble breathing. Call your vet or a pet poison hotline right away.

items.t: Is xylitol toxic to dogs?
items.a: Yes. Xylitol is a sugar free sweetener found in gum, mints, candy, baked goods, toothpaste and some vitamins. In dogs it can cause a dangerous drop in blood sugar, sometimes within 10 to 15 minutes, and liver failure. If your dog eats anything with xylitol, call your vet or a pet poison hotline right away.
